factual_claims.source_evidence: As at 31 December 2025, the Group?s net debt amounted to EUR 432.4 million compared to EUR 537.7 million as at 31 December 2024. The net debt to EBITDA ratio stood at 3.3 as at 31 December 2025 (3.1 as at 31 December 2024).

factual_claims.claim: Proceeds from the sale of three vessels contributed EUR 78.8 million to investing cash flows, supporting a substantial reduction in net debt to EUR 432.4 million from EUR 537.7 million a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net cash flow from investing activities was EUR 46.1 million (EUR 3.2 million in the financial year 2024), including proceeds from disposals of EUR 78.8 million. As at 31 December 2025, the Group?s net debt amounted to EUR 432.4 million compared to EUR 537.7 million as at 31 December 2024.

factual_claims.claim: The equity ratio improved to 56.4% from 53.4%, while the total liquidity buffer stood at EUR 110.4 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Equity ratio? (%) | 56.4% | 53.4% | ... | Total liquidity as at 31 December 2025 | EUR 110.4 million

factual_claims.claim: Operating cash flow remained positive at EUR 127.1 million, though it was partially offset by dividend distributions of EUR 44.6 million and related income taxes of EUR 11.3 million, alongside EUR 113.5 million in loan principal and interest repayments.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group?s net operating cash flow for the financial year 2025 was positive at EUR 127.1 million (EUR 153.4 million in the financial year 2024). The Group?s cash position was impacted by the payment of dividends in the amount of EUR 44.6 million and related income tax of EUR 11.3 million. Total loan repayments and the related interest payments during the financial year amounted to EUR 113.5 million.

factual_claims.claim: Strategic initiatives included optimising fleet utilisation through additional vessel charters, maintaining strict cost discipline, and advancing environmental compliance by preparing to transition shuttle vessels from liquefied natural gas to certified liquefied biomethane.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group continues to focus on cost efficiencies from the previously implemented measures and maintaining profitable operations on its core routes. The Group regularly monitors developments on its core routes, including the capacity of each route, and continues to seek options for chartering vessels that are not used on the main routes and extending existing chartering agreements. Technological development is advancing rapidly, and each scheduled dry-docking enables the Group to bring its vessels up-to-date with the latest standards. One of the most significant steps forward is the imminent large-scale adoption of liquefied biomethane on the Group?s shuttle vessels operating between Tallinn and Helsinki.

factual_claims.claim: Looking ahead, management anticipates continued volatility linked to geopolitical developments, fluctuating energy prices, and restrictive monetary conditions, while reaffirming a commitment to operational resilience, asset efficiency, and sustainable long-term competitiveness.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The key risks for 2026 therefore remain related to geopolitical instability, global trade uncertainty, tax changes, and evolving travel and consumption patterns. The Group recognises the financial risks arising from the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), such as increases in carbon allowance prices, which could lead to higher operating costs and liabilities.
